meta.source: WHO Motor Development Milestones · Capital Institute of Pediatrics Children's Neuropsychological Scale (reference) · Chinese Pediatric Society Developmental Scales · AAP/CDC Milestones (reference)
meta.usage: Used by kid-review for milestone tracking and kid-journal for ability observation. Milestones represent median expectations for most children; individual variation of ±2 months is within normal range.
meta.red_flag_disclaimer: If any red flag (developmental warning sign) appears, please schedule a pediatric developmental assessment promptly. This system does not provide diagnosis.
universal_red_flags: Loss of previously mastered skills at any age (e.g., stops saying words once spoken, stops walking) — seek medical evaluation immediately
At any age: complete absence of eye contact, no smiling at people, persistent lack of response to name
At any age: marked asymmetry between left/right limbs or abnormal muscle tone (excessively stiff or floppy)

items: Lifts head 90 degrees in prone position, raises chest supported on forearms
Holds head briefly steady when held upright
Alternately kicks all four limbs supine, movements becoming coordinated
red_flags: Cannot lift head at all in prone position at 3 months
Head persistently lags severely backward when pulled to sit
Limbs stiff in a scissor pattern or whole body floppy

items: Rolls both ways (prone to supine and back)
Sits leaning forward on forearms or briefly sits unsupported
Legs briefly bear weight when held standing
red_flags: No rolling and no forearm-supported chest raise at 6 months
Head lags markedly and persistently when pulled to sit

items: Sits steadily, can turn head without toppling
Belly crawls or moves backward/forward by inching
Leans forward to reach toys while sitting and returns upright
red_flags: Cannot sit unsupported at 8 months

items: Crawls on hands and knees
Pulls to stand against furniture or using a person
Cruises sideways along furniture
red_flags: No means of self-mobility at 10 months (no crawling, rolling, or scooting)

items: Stands alone momentarily
Walks holding one hand or takes 1-2 independent steps
Lowers from supported standing to sitting independently
red_flags: Cannot pull to stand at 12 months

items: Walks independently with few falls
Squats to pick up a toy and stands back up
Climbs stairs on hands and knees
red_flags: Cannot stand alone at 15 months

items: Walks steadily, can walk backward while pulling a toy
Begins to run (stiff posture is normal)
Throws a ball with arm overhead
red_flags: Not walking independently at 18 months
Persistent toe-walking or markedly abnormal gait

items: Runs steadily, can maneuver around obstacles
Jumps in place with both feet (attempting or mastered)
Climbs stairs one step at a time holding a rail
Kicks a stationary ball
red_flags: Unsteady walking with frequent falls at 2 years
Cannot run or climb stairs with support

items: Jumps in place with both feet, jumps from the last step
Stands on one foot for 1-2 seconds
Climbs stairs alternating feet, one step at a time
Pedals a tricycle
red_flags: Cannot run, falls frequently, or cannot climb stairs at 3 years

items: Hops on one foot several times
Descends stairs alternating feet one step at a time
Catches a large bounced or thrown ball
Standing long jump with both feet
red_flags: Gross motor skills markedly clumsier than peers, unable to join group physical games at 4 years

items: Balances on one foot for 8-10 seconds
Beginning to learn to jump rope
Walks on a low balance beam
Runs, jumps, and dodges moving objects skillfully
red_flags: Cannot hop on one foot; gross motor markedly behind peers at 5 years

items: Consecutive rope jumping
Learning to ride a two-wheel bicycle (may transition from training wheels)
Rhythmically bounces and passes/catches a ball
Can breathe while swimming if lessons started
red_flags: Still unable to combine basic skills of running, jumping, and one-foot standing at 6 years

items: Masters basic skills of 1-2 rule-based ball sports
Can learn coordination sports such as swimming, skating, dance
Strength, speed, and endurance develop in balance; refined motor control
red_flags: Markedly poor coordination and strong avoidance of physical activity at 8 years (consider developmental coordination disorder assessment)

items: Participates in team sports with simple tactical cooperation
Fine and gross motor skills near-adolescent proficiency; fast skill acquisition
Balance, reaction, and coordination approaching adolescent level
red_flags: Still unable to master any sport skill common among peers at 10 years

items: Pubertal growth spurt begins (usually earlier in girls than boys)
Rapid growth in strength and speed; can sustain systematic training
Complex sport combinations (ball tactics, swim strokes, apparatus) near adult beginner level
red_flags: Declining motor ability, asymmetric limp, or persistent pain

items: Hands open naturally, no longer fisted persistently
Looks at own hands (emerging hand-eye coordination)
Grasps a rattle placed in hand (whole-hand grasp) and holds briefly
red_flags: Hands persistently fisted and cannot open at 3 months

items: Reaches out and grasps objects voluntarily (whole-hand grasp)
Transfers object from one hand to the other
Grasps feet and brings them to mouth
red_flags: Does not reach for objects at 6 months
Fixed hand preference appearing at this stage (too-early handedness)

items: Radial-palm grasp (thumb participates)
Holds an object in each hand and bangs them together
Tears paper, pulls at fabric to explore
red_flags: Cannot hold an object in each hand simultaneously at 8 months

items: Picks up small items with neat thumb-index pincer grasp
Deliberately drops and throws objects to observe results
Puts objects into a container
red_flags: Cannot pick up small items with thumb-finger pinch at 10 months

items: Refined pincer grasp for tiny objects
Places blocks into a cup
Scribbles with whole-hand crayon grip
Closes a book (turns several pages at once)
red_flags: No pincer grasp, does not place objects at 12 months

items: Stacks 2 blocks
Spontaneous scribbling
Attempts to use a spoon (spilling is normal)
red_flags: No interest at all in grasping and container play at 15 months

items: Stacks 3-4 blocks
Partially self-feeds with a spoon
Turns doorknobs, opens large jar lids
red_flags: Cannot stack 2 blocks or use a spoon at 18 months

items: Stacks 6 blocks
Imitates drawing vertical lines and circular scribbles
Turns book pages one at a time
Screws and unscrews lids
red_flags: Cannot stack 4 blocks, never scribbles at 2 years

items: Imitates drawing a circle
Stacks 8 or more blocks
Threads large beads onto a string
Draws a person with head and rudimentary limbs (~3.5 years)
red_flags: Cannot stack 6 blocks or imitate drawing lines at 3 years

items: Imitates drawing a cross
Draws a person with 2-4 recognizable parts
Cuts along a straight line with safety scissors
Fastens large buttons independently
red_flags: Cannot hold a crayon to scribble or build a block tower at 4 years

items: Imitates drawing a triangle
Writes some simple characters/letters or a rudimentary own name
Draws a person with 6 or more parts
Learning to tie shoelaces; manages buttons and zippers
red_flags: Drawings still contain no recognizable shapes at 5 years

items: Writes letters, numerals, and simple characters
Cuts out simple shapes with scissors
Uses chopsticks and fork/spoon proficiently
red_flags: Cannot write any recognizable letters/numerals at 6 years

items: Fluent handwriting with gradually consistent size
Completes fine crafts such as origami and model assembly
Keyboard typing, instrument practice (if started)
red_flags: Handwriting persistently illegible with strong writing avoidance at 8 years (consider developmental coordination / dysgraphia assessment)

items: Fine craft skills stable and mature (knitting, woodwork, typing)
Writing speed and quality near the upper childhood range
Specialized skills (instruments, drawing) can deepen
red_flags: Writing still extremely slow and messy with clear learning difficulties at 10 years (assessment recommended)

items: Fine motor skills approaching adult level
Completes complex combined crafts and lab operations
Personalized fluent handwriting; proficient with stationery and tools
red_flags: Marked regression in acquired writing or manipulation skills

items: Coos with vowel sounds
Turns head toward voices and rattling sounds
Cries begin to differentiate (hunger/boredom/discomfort)
red_flags: No reaction to sound at all at 3 months
Never coos

items: Babbles repeated consonant syllables (baba/mama, non-referential)
Laughs out loud
Clear emotional response to tone (stern vs. happy)
red_flags: No big laughs, no consonant syllables at 6 months

items: Responds to own name (turns head/pauses)
Understands 'no' with tone and pauses action
Expresses needs by reaching and vocalizing
red_flags: No response to own name at 8 months
No reaction to familiar daily words (e.g., 'milk')

items: mama/baba becoming referential
Waves bye-bye, claps hands on request
Understands common daily phrases and acts on them
red_flags: No communicative gestures at all (pointing/waving/nodding) at 10 months

items: Says 'mama'/'dada' meaningfully
Uses 1-2 words (milk, give, up)
Follows simple one-step commands ('give the ball to mommy')
Points with index finger to share interest or request
red_flags: No pointing to share, no response to name, no words at 12 months

items: Says 3-5 words
Shakes head for 'no'
Points to common objects in books/pictures
red_flags: Still no meaningful words at 15 months

items: Vocabulary of 10-20 words
Says 'no' to express will
Points to 3 or more body parts
Understands and follows one-step daily instructions
red_flags: Vocabulary limited to mama/dada, does not point to objects at 18 months

items: Two-word phrases ('mommy hold', 'want milk')
Vocabulary over 50 words
Speech ~50% intelligible to strangers
Asks 'What's this?'
red_flags: No two-word phrases at 24 months
Only echoes others' speech without spontaneous communication

items: Speaks 3-4 word sentences
Speech 75%+ intelligible to strangers
Uses pronouns 'I' and 'you'
Endlessly asks 'why'; states own name and age
red_flags: Speech completely unintelligible to strangers at 3 years
Cannot express needs in short sentences

items: Tells simple stories or the day's events
Speech 90%+ intelligible to strangers
Recognizes a few letters or simple characters
Sings complete songs, recites 4+ line nursery rhymes
red_flags: Confusing sentence structure, largely unintelligible at 4 years

items: Mostly complete grammar, fluent sentences
Retells main plot of a story
Print-awareness phase; reads common characters/sight words
Counts to 10+ and counts objects one-to-one
red_flags: Still only short phrases, disorganized narration at 5 years

items: Begins independent reading (decoding/beginner readers)
Describes events in sequence
Vocabulary of thousands; understands time words (yesterday/tomorrow/next week)
red_flags: Marked difficulty with letter/character recognition and sound memory at 6 years (possible early dyslexia signs)

items: Reads chapter books fluently and retells content
Writes paragraphs expressing opinions
Understands metaphors, jokes, and multiple-meaning words
red_flags: Persistent skipping of words/lines in reading, painful avoidance of reading at 8 years (dyslexia assessment recommended)

items: Reads and understands complex narrative and expository texts
Writes multi-paragraph texts with basic structure
Argues points coherently; joins debate-style discussion
red_flags: Huge gap between reading/writing level and oral ability at 10 years (assessment recommended)

items: Understands abstract language (irony, inference, argument)
Produces argumentative writing
Can systematically learn foreign languages
red_flags: Marked regression in language/literacy with attention or mood problems (assessment recommended)

items: Social smile (smiles at people, not spontaneous sleep smiles)
Gazes at faces for long periods, prefers eyes
Responds to playful interaction with sounds and waving limbs
red_flags: No social smile at 3 months
Complete lack of interest in faces

items: Excited by mirror image, pats mirror
Imitates tongue protrusion, mouth opening and other expressions
Looks down for dropped objects (emerging object permanence)
Stranger awareness begins (gradually evident 6-9 months)
red_flags: No interest in mirror or faces at 6 months
No response to interactive games (proto peek-a-boo)

items: Searches for fully hidden toys (object permanence developing)
Enjoys peek-a-boo and anticipates the reveal
Separation anxiety appears (normal attachment behavior)
red_flags: No differential reaction to caregivers vs. strangers combined with no interest in hiding games at 8 months (observe holistically)

items: Imitates social gestures like clapping and waving
Uses objects functionally (brushes hair with comb, drinks from cup)
Repeatedly empties containers to explore cause and effect
red_flags: Imitates no actions at 10 months
No functional object exploration (only bangs/bites/throws)

items: Joint attention: points plus eye contact to share interest
Shows or points to you before requesting help
Functional toy play (pushes car, stacks tower, presses buttons)
red_flags: No pointing to share interest, no joint attention at 12 months
Little eye contact, does not seek engagement

items: Emerging pretend play (feeds doll with spoon)
Imitates household chores (sweeping, wiping)
Clear willingness to self-feed with spoon
red_flags: No signs of pretend play at 15 months
Lack of eye contact and shared enjoyment

items: Points to distant desired objects to express needs
Parallel play (plays beside peers, not yet cooperatively)
Emerging self-awareness (says 'mine', recognizes self in mirror)
Helps with simple tasks (hands over items)
red_flags: No pretend play, no eye contact at 18 months
Persistent avoidance of interaction and being addressed

items: Rich pretend play (pretend cooking, phone calls)
Imitates adults' gross actions and daily routines
Attends to peers; simple interactions emerge
Strong self-awareness and possessiveness; 'no' phase
red_flags: No pretend play at 24 months; only repetitive object manipulation
No interaction or eye contact with anyone; does not follow instructions

items: Turn-taking games, emerging rule awareness
Role-play imagination games (doctor, cook)
Shows empathy (comforts a crying peer)
Knows own gender, names family relationships
red_flags: No imaginative play at 3 years
No interest in peers; no turn-taking interaction at all

items: Cooperative play toward shared goals with peers
Tells invented stories, assigns roles in play
Understands and follows simple game rules
Names emotions: happy/angry/sad
red_flags: Cannot understand any rules or join group games at 4 years

items: Has 1-2 stable friends; 'best friend' concept
Follows game rules; copes with simple winning/losing
Emerging perspective-taking ('he is sad')
Tidies own toys and belongings
red_flags: Cannot form friendships at all; persistently rejected by peers at 5 years (monitor closely)

items: Understands others may hold different views and feelings
Managing winning/losing emotions (learning, still needs adult guidance)
Adapts to group activities and classroom routines
Emerging executive function: two-step instructions, delayed gratification
red_flags: Cannot follow classroom routines at all; frequent uncontrolled social conflicts at 6 years

items: Executive function: plans simple tasks, completes homework in steps (with reminders)
Stable friendships and peer groups
Understands fairness, rules, and right vs. wrong logically
Time concepts established (clock time, durations)
red_flags: No friendships at all, persistent social avoidance or bullying at 8 years (assessment and intervention recommended)

items: Peer relationships central to emotional life; values belonging
Team collaboration and division of labor
Logical thinking: concrete causality, classification, simple reasoning
Self-evaluation forms; cares about grades and recognition
red_flags: Persistent peer difficulties with low mood and school refusal at 10 years (professional assessment recommended)

items: Abstract and hypothetical reasoning (Piaget formal operational stage begins)
Strong peer identification; values group norms
Identity exploration; critical thinking about authority
Executive function near adult: multitasking, long-range planning
red_flags: Persistent low mood, complete social withdrawal, cliff-drop grades in adolescence (psychological assessment recommended)
